doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Three years with Lucky Millinder and Irving Mills's displeasure
summary: Millinder's band took what Duke and Cab did not want, and Millinder lost favour with Mills over money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You had gotten stranded, and you came back to New York.

I’m with Lucky Millinder for three years. We played everything between Duke and Cab. What they didn’t want, they shove in Lucky Millinder. Irving Mills was handling Lucky Millinder for a while. Lucky Millinder mess up with the money. Drank it. Throwed it away in the salary. They got mad with him. Said, “We got to get rid of this monkey.” So he never was a success no more, because you couldn’t trust him to bring the salary back in. That was the end of . . . So I’m with Lucky Millinder’s band. Lucky
